default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-388.title: Round-trip-hour micro-break fade
E-388.hypothesis: When the close is back near where it was an hour ago (net hourly change small next to its usual size at this minute), the hour's buyers and sellers have cancelled out and nobody holds a directional parent order; a short-term break of the recent high/low in that state is a local push that the two-way hour absorbs, so fade it (rolling-hour net change, not the move from the open or the VWAP slope).

E-389.title: Counter-leg micro-break fade
E-389.hypothesis: An up-break of the recent short-term high made while the close is still in the lower part of the last two hours' range is a relief rally inside a larger down leg: short covering triggers it, while the sellers who built the two-hour leg still hold inventory and sell into the bounce; fade it (mirror for down-breaks high in the two-hour range).

E-390.title: Day-after-inside-day micro-break fade
E-390.hypothesis: A session whose whole range stayed inside the session before it was a contraction day: other-timeframe traders did not initiate and the two-day range is the frame everyone trades; the next session's short-term breaks happen inside that balance, without new initiative behind them, and revert as responsive traders lean on them.

E-391.title: Double-tested box break fade
E-391.hypothesis: A recent box whose top AND bottom were each touched at least twice is a rectangle that both sides defend with resting orders; the first close through one edge mostly fills the stops parked just beyond it, after which the defenders who held the edge twice re-establish it, so the break reverts into the box.

E-392.title: Volatile-tape micro-break fade (liquidity-provision premium)
E-392.hypothesis: Nagel: the return to providing liquidity (short-term reversal) rises sharply when volatility is high, because intermediaries withdraw and the remaining liquidity is priced dearly; when the last half hour's range is far above its usual size at this minute, short-term breaks are demand for immediacy into a thin book, so fading them earns that elevated premium.

E-393.title: Ease-of-Movement threshold cross follow
E-393.hypothesis: Arms' Ease of Movement measures how far the bar midpoint moves per contract traded; when its smoothed value crosses a clear threshold, price is rising (falling) with little volume needed, i.e. the opposite side has stepped back from the book; while that withdrawal lasts the move continues, so follow the cross.

E-394.title: Doji-regime micro-break fade
E-394.hypothesis: When recent sessions have mostly closed near where they opened (small average daily body versus daily range), each day's excursions are given back by the close: the market is in a multi-day regime where intraday pushes are taken back by responsive traders; short-term breaks in such a regime are faded (daily open-to-close body share, not daily return autocorrelation or today's own candle).

E-395.title: Opening half-hour micro-break fade
E-395.hypothesis: In the first minutes after the open the book is still being rebuilt after the auction and liquidity is thinnest, so overnight orders arriving piecemeal push small boxes back and forth; a short-term break in that window is order-arrival noise that the market makers re-quoting the book pull back, so fade it until the opening period is over.

E-396.title: Snap-back break fade
E-396.hypothesis: A close through the recent high printed right after a clearly down bar is a V-shaped snap: the break comes from a one-bar reversal of a selling bar (stops of the dip sellers plus a burst of market buys), not from a build-up of buyers; the urgent orders are spent within the bar and the box's sellers return, so fade it (mirror after an up bar).

E-397.title: Chaikin oscillator threshold cross follow
E-397.hypothesis: The Chaikin oscillator (fast minus slow EMA of today's accumulation/distribution line) turns when volume starts closing bars on the other side of their ranges; a cross beyond a clear threshold means accumulation (distribution) is accelerating, a parent order being worked through the session, which keeps pushing for a while, so follow it.
